title: CeO2-Based Nanoparticles Immobilizing on Chitosan Films, Studied by Different Microscopy Techniques
content: Immobilizing nanomaterials on a substrate allows their application in different fields. The development of food packaging with metal oxide nanoparticles (NPs) as an antimicrobial agent is a nanotechnology application technology that reduces food waste due to microbial spoilage, economic losses in the food industry, and foodborne diseases [1]. The antimicrobial activity of these packages depends on their physicochemical properties, such as the interaction of the nanoparticles with the support matrix. This interaction is responsible for releasing the antimicrobial agent into the surrounding environment. Therefore, it is important to study the distribution and interaction of the nanoparticles with the substrate, and microscopy techniques are a tool for this purpose [2].
